bib.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness", Huatong Song* and Fei Bai* (equal first authors; Renmin Univ. of China, IQuest Research), with Wayne Xin Zhao and Mingjie Tang as corresponding authors. arXiv:2608.16798v1 [cs.CL], 17 Aug 2026. Preprint, no venue.
COVERAGE: 20 of 20 pages read; 67,216 of 67,216 chars. References were skimmed only. Appendix A (the judge prompt) was read. There is no other appendix.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Black-box RL through OpenClaw and Claude Code improves Qwen3-30A3B. ClawGym-Bench Pass@1 rises 9.98 points (OpenClaw) and 14.81 points (Claude Code).
 number: +9.98 and +14.81. Table 1 averages: OpenClaw 45.11 -> 62.62, Claude Code 37.06 -> 51.87. PinchBench: +11.71 and +17.28.
 setup: Qwen3-8B and 30A3B; training tasks from ClawGym-SynData; context 64K; one run per cell, with no seeds or variance reported. ClawII-OC starts from a lightly SFT'd "Cold" model. ClawII-CC starts from the base model. Judge is GPT-5.4 with 0.7 code / 0.3 rubric weights. PinchBench is a 30-task text-only subset.
 quote: "ClawII-OC and ClawII-CC outperform their respective initial policies by 9.98 and 14.81 points on ClawGym-Bench under OpenClaw and Claude Code, respectively."
 where: p.11
 Bears on: 05 (post-training for agents).
2. After training, the 30A3B models beat Qwen3-235A23B in the matching harness. The 8B models gain 7.92 (OC) and 23.51 (CC) points. Under OpenClaw, the RL model beats the ClawGym-30A3B SFT baseline.
 number: +8.14 and +6.28 over 235B; +5.80 over SFT (62.62 vs 56.82)
 setup: same as claim 1. The SFT baseline is ClawGym-30A3B. OpenClaw is the only harness with an SFT baseline.
 quote: "The resulting 30A3B models further outperform Qwen3-235A23B by 8.14 and 6.28 points in the two settings"
 where: p.11
 Bears on: 05, 06.
3. White-box AgentLoop RL beats black-box RL in-loop, but transfers worse to OpenClaw.
 number: AgentLoop average 59.90 vs 51.37 for the OpenClaw-trained model (+8.53). WhiteBox-30A3B gets 50.33 under OpenClaw (+5.22 over base 45.11) vs 62.62 for ClawII-OC.
 setup: Qwen3-30A3B; the AgentLoop has 5 tool categories (bash, search, fetch, code interpreter, file ops); same data and eval. This is the only baseline or ablation of black-box against an alternative design.
 quote: "WhiteBox-30A3B still falls behind ClawII-OC-30A3B, which is trained directly under OpenClaw and achieves 62.62, revealing that training under a simple white-box agentloop may still be insufficient to fully capture the harness-specific interaction patterns"
 where: p.16
 Bears on: 05, 10.
4. Mix-harness training (GRPO, OC+CC jointly) matches or slightly beats single-harness training. Advantages are normalised per task-harness group.
 number: none given as a table; shown only in Fig 4 curves (50-300 steps)
 setup: Qwen3-30A3B from base, no cold start; 32 task-harness instances x 8 rollouts; eval on ClawGym-Bench.
 quote: "combining rollouts from heterogeneous harnesses introduces no evident training instability or systematic performance degradation."
 where: p.13
 Bears on: 05, 10.
5. PPO and GRPO are both stable for 200-400 steps with comparable final results. The comparison is matched on rollout budget per update. PPO needs value pretraining.
 number: GRPO 32 tasks x 8 rollouts; PPO 256 tasks x 1 rollout
 setup: Qwen3-30A3B; the OpenClaw runs start from cold start and the Claude Code runs from base, so harness and init are confounded. PPO has smoother entropy. GRPO has larger variation, including a late entropy decline under OC.
 quote: "GRPO uses batches of 32 tasks with 8 rollouts per task, while PPO uses batches of 256 tasks with 1 rollout per task, resulting in the same rollout budget per update."
 where: p.12
 Bears on: 05, 07, 10.
6. The method extends to harder tasks with synthesized training data.
 number: JobBench-Easy 20.46 -> 27.20; OfficeQA-Full 8.53 -> 21.54
 setup: Qwen3-30A3B, Claude Code harness, synthesized JobBench-style and OfficeQA-style tasks; training tasks are an (instruction, workspace, verifier) triplet.
 quote: "evaluation performance improves from 20.46 to 27.20 on JobBench-Easy and from 8.53 to 21.54 on OfficeQA-Full."
 where: p.14
 Bears on: 06 (data and environments), 07.
7. Cold start (lightweight SFT on a ClawGym-SynData subset) helps but is not required. The cold-started run has higher starting reward, smoother entropy and better eval. The base-init run has a "pronounced late-stage entropy decline". No numbers are given; Fig 7 is the only evidence.
 setup: Qwen3-30A3B, OpenClaw, GRPO.
 where: p.14
 Bears on: 05, 08 (entropy behaviour).
8. Method design (the engineering content).
 - Sandbox per rollout.
 - A serving proxy at the model boundary records the exact tokens and logprobs.
 - Model calls are organised into a prefix tree. Dead (retry) leaves, over-branching rollouts and subagent/compaction trajectories are dropped. Only main-agent trajectories train.
 - All trajectories from a rollout share the terminal reward. Shared-prefix tokens count once.
 - PPO is simplified to gamma=lambda=1, so the advantage is R_i - V(s_t).
 - Token-in-token-out plus token-level truncated importance-sampling correction w_t = min(exp(log pi_old - log pi_rollout), c).
 - Safeguards: timeouts, discarding sandbox failures, buffered pseudo-streaming tool-call parsing, and waiting for trajectory records to "settle".
 where: pp.5-10
 Bears on: 10 (engineering RL systems), 07 (reward is a final-workspace verifier, rule-based or rubric/LLM judge).

LIMITS
- Training-inference consistency and the prefix-tree filters are described but never ablated. No ablation of tree vs per-call, IS correction vs none, or the safeguards.
- No seeds or confidence intervals. All numbers come from single runs.
- Confounds: the OC runs are warm-started and the CC runs are not. No cold-start-vs-none table exists. Only the training curves show the effect.
- Auxiliary (subagent and compaction) trajectories are excluded. The authors defer them to future work.
- The PPO simplification may "increase advantage variance". The authors leave a proper treatment of forked trajectories to future work.
- Only Qwen3 models (8B, 30A3B) were trained. Only two harnesses and one data source were used. Judge is GPT-5.4 only.
- White-box in-loop beats black-box (claim 3). The paper concedes that black-box-trained models do not beat white-box models on the white-box loop.
- Mix-harness numbers are curves only. There is no final-score table.
- Wall-clock, throughput and cost are not reported.
- The text shows no contamination check between ClawGym-SynData and ClawGym-Bench (same group's data).

BUILDS ON: PPO (Schulman et al. [25]), GRPO (Shao et al. [26]), ReAct (Yao et al. 2022), ClawGym (Bai et al. 2026, arXiv:2604.26904; supplies data and benchmark), token-in-token-out (Gallouedec and Rasul, May 2026 blog), the training-inference mismatch and IS correction work (Liu et al. 2025 blog [15]; Yao et al. 2025 blog [34]), prefix trees (KAT-Coder-V2 [12]), Dressage [11] and OpenForgeRL [37] for black-box harness RL. Author names for [25], [26] and [34] were not checked in the extracted text.

CODE: none. Equations only: Eq. 8 (A_t = R_i - V(s_t)) and Eq. 10 (token-level truncated IS weight).

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p.6: pipeline of sandbox, proxy, prefix tree, filtering and RL update. It is the fastest way to see the architecture.
- Fig 2, 3, 8 (pp.12, 12, 16): PPO vs GRPO reward, entropy and eval curves for OC, CC and AgentLoop.
- Fig 4, p.13: mix-harness vs single-harness.
- Fig 7, p.15: cold start vs no cold start.
- Figs 5, 6, p.14: JobBench and OfficeQA.

PROBLEMS: Tables and figure axes extracted as flat text, so Table 1 column alignment is partly inferred. Bold and underline marks are lost. Some cells have run together, e.g. "61.3967.33". The caption text is clear. The paper contains no embedded instructions. The "{{USER_TASK}}" placeholders in Appendix A are only template text for the judge prompt.
